messages:
olivia: Quick follow-up from the iterator surface RFC — can we sync on tradeoffs for streaming vs. paged transports? I'm worried about ergonomic fragmentation across py/ts/go.
chao: +1. main questions: resume semantics (opaque token vs structured cursor), retry idempotency, and whether streaming iterator yields partial pages or single items.
sarah: From SDK POV I'd prefer a single iterator abstraction: next() yields items, underlying transport can be streaming chunks or page fetches. keep cursor opaque to consumers.
raj: Agreed on opaque cursor for flexibility, but we must standardize resume token expiry and validation.
olivia: For languages: python iterator vs ts async iterable vs go channel. We need comparable cancellation semantics and backoff hooks.
chao: Proposal: expose cancel/close on all clients; async iterables in TS map to __anext__/for-await; python generator with close(); go provide an Iterator{Next() (T, error); Close() error}.
sarah: Retry rules: server-provided resume token must allow restart from last confirmed emitted item. If transport is streaming, we still checkpoint per page boundary.
raj: Implementation note: streaming transports should emit explicit 'checkpoint' markers in stream (control frames) so SDK can persist tokens without guessing.
olivia: Example API sketch (python):
```
with client.responses.list(prompt) as it:
    for item in it:
        process(item)
```
We need close() to flush and optionally persist token.
chao: TS equivalent sample:
```ts
for await (const msg of client.responses.stream("hi")) {
  handle(msg)
}
```
Add .stop() for manual close.
raj: Backoff: client should not retry non-idempotent requests automatically. For list/stream we can retry on transport errors if we have a valid resume token; otherwise bubble up error for manual retry.
sarah: Edge-case: what about partial page replays when token points into page? We should force server to provide page-aligned tokens only to keep SDK simple.
olivia: That simplifies invariants. Server: ensure token semantics are page-aligned and stable across minor model-version rollouts.
chao: Action items:
  • eng-runtime: add stream checkpoint frames (raj)
  • api: document opaque token lifetime and "pageAligned": true (sarah)
  • sdks: implement Close/Cancel patterns and token persistence hooks (olivia, kai)
raj: I'll open runtime PR for checkpoint frames today.
kai: I'll prototype Go iterator pattern and surface it in SDKs repo.
deploy-bot: deploy started: transport-checkpoints/PR-412
olivia: Thanks — will follow up in PR comments. :thumbsup:
